Toilet Repairs and Installation Across the Inner West

Most toilet faults are fixed in one visit with parts from the van.

Toilet repairs fix a toilet that is blocked, keeps running, leaks into the bowl or at the base, or will not flush properly, usually by replacing a worn part rather than the whole toilet. Our licensed plumbers repair and install toilets in houses, terraces and apartments across the Inner West, and clear the drain behind them when that is the problem.

What is wrong with your toilet?

Most toilet problems come down to a handful of parts. A running toilet usually has a worn inlet valve or flush valve seal, a leaking toilet at the base has a failed seal or pan connector, and a weak flush often points to the button or the valve. Match what you see to the usual fix below.

Guide only. The plumber confirms the cause on site before replacing anything.
What you noticeUsual causeUsual fix
Cistern keeps filling or hissingInlet valve not shutting offReplace the inlet valve
Water trickles into the bowlWorn flush valve sealReplace the seal or flush valve
Water on the floor around the baseFailed pan connector or sealReseal or replace the connector
Water rises when you flushBlockage in the pan or the drainClear the pan, or the drain beyond it
Weak or half flush onlyButton, cable or valve faultAdjust or replace the flush parts
Cistern slow to refillPartly closed isolating tap or a tired valveOpen or replace the tap or valve

Blocked toilet: the toilet or the drain?

A blocked toilet on its own is usually a blockage in the pan or the pipe just behind it. If the shower drains slowly too, other fixtures gurgle, or water rises in the yard gully, the blockage is further down the drain. The fix is different, so it helps to know which one you have.

Just the toilet

Paper, wipes or an object stuck in the pan's trap. A plunger may clear it; if not, we clear the pan without damaging it.

Several fixtures at once

The shared drain is blocked, often by roots in an old clay pipe. That is a drain job, covered on our page about clearing blocked sewer drains.

Wipes, even flushable ones

Wipes do not break down like toilet paper. They are one of the most common causes of blocked toilets we clear.

Skip the chemicals

Drain chemicals rarely shift a toilet blockage and can damage old pipes and seals. Stop flushing and call us instead.

Two quick checks for a leaking toilet

A toilet leaking into the bowl is easy to miss, because the water trickles quietly down the back of the pan. Sydney Water says a leaking toilet can waste as much as 260 litres a day. These two checks take a minute and tell you whether your cistern is leaking.

  • The paper test: put a sheet of dry toilet paper against the back of the bowl, above the water line. If it is damp before anyone flushes, the cistern is leaking.
  • The dye test: add a few drops of food colouring to the cistern and do not flush for 15 minutes. Colour in the bowl means a leak.
  • Listen: a properly working cistern is silent between flushes. Any hiss or trickle means a valve is not shutting off.
  • Check the meter: if the toilet is leaking, the water meter will move even when nothing else is running.

If the toilet checks out but the meter still moves, the leak is somewhere else, and our hidden water leak detection page explains how we find it.

Toilet installation and replacement

Toilet installation starts with measuring the set-out, the distance from the wall to the waste pipe, because that decides which toilets will fit. Older Inner West terraces often have unusual set-outs. We remove the old toilet, fit the new one with a new connector and isolating tap, and test it.

  1. Measure the set-out

    Wall to waste pipe, and whether the outlet goes into the floor or the wall.

  2. Remove the old toilet

    Isolate the water, take out the old pan and cistern, clean up the waste pipe.

  3. Fit the new toilet

    New pan connector, new seal and a new isolating tap for the cistern.

  4. Test and seal

    Several flushes to check for leaks, then seal the base neatly.

Choosing a new toilet? Sydney Water notes that older single flush toilets use 11 litres a flush, while modern dual flush toilets use 4.5 litres for a full flush and 3 litres for a half flush.

How much does a plumber charge to install a toilet?

What a plumber charges to install a toilet depends on whether it is a straight swap, how the waste pipe is set up, and whether the floor or wall needs work. Most toilet repairs cost less than a replacement, so we tell you if a part will fix the old one. You agree the price before we start.

  1. Repair or replaceA new valve or seal costs far less than a new toilet.
  2. Straight swap or changeA like-for-like toilet replacement is quicker than changing the outlet type.
  3. Set-out and waste pipeAn unusual set-out may need an offset connector or pipe changes.
  4. Floor and wallTiles that need patching after the old pan comes out add time.
  5. TimingA blocked toilet at night or on a weekend costs more than a weekday booking.

Toilet repair questions

What people ask about blocked, running and leaking toilets. Anything else, call 0412 395 426.

Why does my toilet keep running?

A running toilet usually has an inlet valve that does not shut off, so the cistern keeps filling, or a worn flush valve seal that lets water slip into the bowl, so the cistern keeps topping up. Both are common parts we carry and replace in one visit.

Can I clear a blocked toilet with a plunger?

Often, yes, if the blockage is in the pan itself. Use a plunger made for toilets and stop flushing so it does not overflow. If it will not clear, or other drains are slow too, the blockage is further down and needs a plumber.

Why is water leaking around the base of my toilet?

Water at the base usually comes from a failed pan connector or seal where the toilet meets the waste pipe, or from a leaking cistern connection dripping down. A leak at the base can damage the floor over time, so it is worth fixing early.

Can you install a toilet I have already bought?

Yes. Check the set-out before you buy if you can, because the distance from the wall to the waste pipe decides which toilets fit. If the one you bought does not suit the pipe, we tell you before we start rather than after.

Is it worth repairing an old toilet?

A sound pan with a worn valve or seal is worth repairing, and it is usually a quick job. An old single flush toilet with a cracked pan, or parts that are no longer made, is usually better replaced with a water-efficient dual flush model.

Are flushable wipes safe for toilets?

We advise against them. Wipes do not break down like toilet paper and are one of the most common things we pull out of blocked toilets and drains, especially in older clay sewer pipes with roots at the joints.

Do you repair toilets in apartments and strata buildings?

Yes. The toilet itself is usually the lot owner's responsibility in an NSW strata building, while the shared drain behind the wall is common property. We tell you which part the fault is in so the right party is billed.
